external/claude-code-hooks.txt

WHAT THIS IS
  The hook settings in each laptop's demo-app clone: <clone>/.claude/settings.local.json. They tell
  Claude Code to run our hook scripts (repo 1, hooks/src/*.ts). The file holds absolute paths, so
  it's per laptop and gitignored. hooks/src/install.ts writes it.

WHO / WHEN
  A: first version Sat 9:20. Everyone runs install on their own laptop before checkpoint 2 (Sat 19:00).

TONIGHT, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE
  hooks/src/rewake-spike.ts proves that an asyncRewake hook wakes an idle session. The whole design
  depends on it. Instructions are in that file's header.

WHAT GETS REGISTERED
  event              matcher                                 script                 options
  PostToolUse        Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Bash  snapshot-and-wait.ts   asyncRewake, timeout 1800
  PostToolUse        *                                       inject-context.ts      timeout 5
  UserPromptSubmit   (none)                                  inject-context.ts      timeout 5
  Stop               (none)                                  stop.ts                timeout 5
  SessionStart       (none)                                  session-start.ts       timeout 10
  Each one in exec form: "command": "node", "args": ["<absolute path to the .ts file>"].
  Print the exact block for your laptop with:  node hooks/src/install.ts

CHECK IT WORKS
  - In a Claude session in the clone, /hooks lists all of them.
  - Make an edit: a wip/<you> branch appears on GitHub within about 2 seconds.
  - Debugging: set COWORK_DEBUG=1 in repo 1's .env so hook errors print to stderr, and start
    Claude Code with --debug to see every hook run.

FACTS WE RELY ON (Claude Code hooks reference, checked Oct 24)
  - asyncRewake runs the hook in the background. Exit code 2 wakes Claude immediately, even when the
    session is idle, and stderr is shown to Claude. Unlike plain async hooks, its timeout IS enforced.
  - Stop hooks receive stop_hook_active. Claude Code stops honoring blocks after 8 in a row.
  - Matcher "*" (or no matcher) means every tool. UserPromptSubmit, Stop and SessionStart need none.
  - Exec form (command + args) runs with no shell, so paths with spaces or backslashes are safe.
  - Node 24 runs .ts files directly, so hooks need no build step.
